moat_against: Limited pricing power — earnings are a market-set buy/sell spread that mean-reverts
Low switching barriers — customers can dual-source; DSV, Kuehne+Nagel and DHL match or exceed its scale
Cyclical trade exposure — Asia-North America lanes, tariffs and geopolitics drive results
moat_for: Network effect — dense global office and trade-lane network in a fragmented industry
Customs brokerage and regulatory expertise — sticky, high-value work as tariffs tighten
Asset-light model — structurally low capex and capacity flexibility in volatile rate markets
Cohesive organic culture with profit-linked branch compensation and industry-leading profitability
moat_justification: A dense global network and customs expertise give Expeditors a real, durable edge and high returns on capital through the cycle, but forwarding itself has limited pricing power — the buy/sell spread is set by the freight market, customers can multi-source, and equally scaled rivals exist.
name: EXPEDITORS INTERNATIONAL OF WASHINGTON, INC.
one_liner: High-quality asset-light forwarder with a strong moat (7/10), but at $196.38 it clears nothing — weighted IRR 7.3%, IV@15% $70.55, and even the super-bull case stays below the price; it would need to fall to $70.55 or below to clear the 15% hurdle on the weighted case.
